title: Three Little Words: Lester remembers a Freeman trio record
summary: Freeman tells how Lester asked to hear his Trio album twice on 52nd Street and, in 1946, greeted him saying 'Three Little Words was a bitch.'

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, again, Helen, may I preface this by saying I am always frightened of talking too much about myself -- I don't mean to, but just to tell it because there is a relationship [between Lester and myself.]
This story about Lester, speaking of the nature of the man. He was very deep and very bright and conserved words as he did notes, to make beautiful sentences, and he -- I had made -- now, let's see.

I had left Goodman and Lester had left Basie just about the same time and I ran into Lester in 52nd Street, Gabler had the Commodore Music Shop, and I ran into Lester and I said, 'Would you come in and hear a Trio album that I just made -- it was the one I made with Jess Stacy and George Wettling and Three Little Words was on the album and so we played it, and Lester said, 'Oh, could I hear that again, and I said, 'Thank you, I am very delighted you like it.'

So we played it all over again and he started singing and whistling phrases from it. Now, I was not to see Lester again until -- let's see, that would have been I think I left Benny, about the end of '38 maybe '39. I hope that is the right year, although I don't think it matters too much.
I was not to see Lester again until I went to Chicago and got lost in the war and I came out of the war

and I came to New York and that -- I got out of the war just about a month after it ended, August of 1945, and I ran into Lester again in '46 and of all places, would you believe it, 52nd Street. He's going the same way. He was going toward 6th Avenue, I was going towards 5th, and before he said, 'Hello, Bud, how are you,' he said, 'That Three Little Words was a bitch.' Now, you think of the memory of this, again not because it was about me, but the lovely thing to remember.
I told that to -- who is the bass player who has such a marvelous collection of Lester Young stories, is it Gene Ramey?
Well, I remember running into him at one of those jazz festivals in Colorado and I told him that story about Lester and he just fell out laughing and then he told me a beautiful story about Lester.
